lion.definition: (astrology) a person who is born while the sun is in Leo.

elephant.definition: A very large mammal with a trunk, tusks, and wide ears.

giraffe.definition: A tall African mammal with a very long neck and spotted coat.

zebra.definition: Any of several fleet black-and-white striped African equines.

hippo.definition: An ancient Numidian town in northwestern Africa adjoining present-day Annaba in northeastern Algeria.

rhino.definition: Massive powerful herbivorous odd-toed ungulate of southeast Asia and Africa having very thick skin and one or two horns on the snout.

buffalo.definition: Any of several Old World animals resembling oxen including, e.g., water buffalo, Cape buffalo.
buffalo.exampleUsage: The buffalo was identified during the lesson.

cheetah.definition: Long-legged spotted cat of Africa and southwestern Asia having nonretractile claws.

leopard.definition: A large wild cat with a spotted coat.

wildebeest.definition: Large African antelope having a head with horns like an ox and a long tufted tail.

meerkat.definition: A mongoose-like viverrine of South Africa having a face like a lemur and only four toes.

warthog.definition: African wild swine with warty protuberances on the face and large protruding tusks.

hyena.definition: Doglike nocturnal mammal of Africa and southern Asia that feeds chiefly on carrion.
hyena.exampleUsage: The hyena was identified during the lesson.

jackal.definition: A jackal native to Europe and Asia with a golden coat.

baboon.definition: Large terrestrial monkeys having doglike muzzles.

gazelle.definition: Small swift graceful antelope of Africa and Asia having lustrous eyes.

impala.definition: African antelope with ridged curved horns.

ostrich.definition: A person who refuses to face reality or recognize the truth (a reference to the popular notion that the ostrich hides from danger by burying its head in the sand).

vulture.definition: Any of various large diurnal birds of prey having naked heads and weak claws and feeding chiefly on carrion.
vulture.exampleUsage: The vulture was identified during the lesson.

grassland.definition: Land where grass or grasslike vegetation grows and is the dominant form of plant life.

acacia-tree.definition: A tree or shrub of warm dry regions, often with small leaves and sometimes thorns.
acacia-tree.exampleUsage: An acacia tree provided shade on the open savanna.

baobab.definition: African tree having an exceedingly thick trunk and fruit that resembles a gourd and has an edible pulp called monkey bread.

termite-mound.definition: A raised structure of soil built by a colony of termites as a nest.
termite-mound.exampleUsage: A tall termite mound stood beside the grassland.

watering-hole.definition: A natural pool or shallow lake that provides wild animals with a place to drink.
watering-hole.exampleUsage: The watering hole was identified during the lesson.

horizon.definition: The range of interest or activity that can be anticipated.

sunset.definition: The time in the evening at which the sun begins to fall below the horizon.

dry-riverbed.definition: The channel where a river flows at wetter times but currently contains little or no water.
dry-riverbed.exampleUsage: Animals crossed the dry riverbed during the dry season.

kopje.definition: A small hill rising up from the African veld.

dust.definition: Fine powdery material such as dry earth or pollen that can be blown about in the air.

flamingo.definition: Large pink to scarlet web-footed wading bird with down-bent bill.
flamingo.exampleUsage: The flamingo was identified during the lesson.

eagle.definition: Any of various large keen-sighted diurnal birds of prey noted for their broad wings and strong soaring flight.
eagle.exampleUsage: The eagle was identified during the lesson.

stork.definition: Large mostly Old World wading birds typically having white-and-black plumage.
stork.exampleUsage: The stork was identified during the lesson.

weaver-bird.definition: A small bird known for weaving grass or plant fibers into complex hanging nests.
weaver-bird.exampleUsage: A weaver bird was building a nest in the acacia tree.

hornbill.definition: Bird of tropical Africa and Asia having a very large bill surmounted by a bony protuberance.
hornbill.exampleUsage: The hornbill was identified during the lesson.

secretary-bird.definition: A tall African bird of prey with long legs that hunts mainly on the ground.
secretary-bird.exampleUsage: The secretary bird walked through the grass searching for prey.

guinea-fowl.definition: A ground-dwelling African bird with a rounded body and spotted or patterned feathers.
guinea-fowl.exampleUsage: A group of guinea fowl crossed the savanna.

kingfisher.definition: Nonpasserine large-headed bird with a short tail and long sharp bill.
kingfisher.exampleUsage: The kingfisher was identified during the lesson.

crane.definition: A tall machine with a long arm used to lift heavy materials.
crane.exampleUsage: The crane was used during the activity.

heron.definition: Grey or white wading bird with long neck and long legs and (usually) long bill.
heron.exampleUsage: The heron was identified during the lesson.

jeep.definition: A car suitable for traveling over rough terrain.

binoculars.definition: An instrument used for seeing distant objects more clearly.
binoculars.exampleUsage: The binoculars was used during the activity.

camera.definition: Equipment for taking photographs (usually consisting of a lightproof box with a lens at one end and light-sensitive film at the other).

guide.definition: A person who can find paths through unexplored territory.

tent.definition: A temporary shelter made from fabric and supported by poles.

campfire.definition: An outdoor fire built for warmth, cooking, or light.

ranger.definition: A member of the Texas state highway patrol.

tracks.definition: (computer science) one of the circular magnetic paths on a magnetic disk that serve as a guide for writing and reading data.

map.definition: A drawing that shows places, routes, and geographical features.

sunhat.definition: A hat with a broad brim that protects the face from direct exposure to the sun.

predator.definition: A person who attacks in search of booty.

prey.definition: A person who is the aim of an attack (especially a victim of ridicule or exploitation) by some hostile person or influence.

herd.definition: A group of wild mammals of one species that remain together: antelope or elephants or seals or whales or zebra.
herd.exampleUsage: The herd was identified during the lesson.

migration.definition: The movement of persons from one country or locality to another.

drought.definition: A long period with very little or no rain.

rainy-season.definition: One of the two main seasons in tropical climates, marked by frequent rainfall.
rainy-season.arabicTranslation: كائن أو عنصر طبيعي يُسمّى «رايني سياسون»

food-chain.definition: A linked series of organisms in an ecosystem transfers energy and nutrients as each member consumes the one before it.

camouflage.definition: Colors or patterns that help an animal blend into its surroundings.

territory.definition: An area of knowledge or interest.

den.exampleUsage: The den was identified during the lesson.
